lesson: The rank-one or rank-two update the assignment asked for does not exist: the pole is rank one on the Bezoutian L but rank 2d on L(x)L, and the crossing points that carry the negative squares in general position degenerate exactly on the symmetric locus. Passing to the orthogonal sign-free kernel N+ turns positivity of a rank d(d-1)/2 form into counting d negative squares of a one-variable three-term kernel. Practical: the server ran about three times slower than the Mac under load; six local d = 16 workers exceed the 8 GB cap.
followUp: Prove NL(d): for symmetric g (g(-1-u) = g(u), zeros in the strip) the three-term kernel N+((1,z),(1,z')) built from g(z+1), g(z), g(z-1) has d negative squares. Equivalent pair: N is positive on the pole line, and N+ has rank at least d+1 there. This closes X(d) and row D10 via c18 Proposition L3 (model sense only). A referee pass on Lemma 1 and Theorems 2 to 4 is owed.
